THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 22.7.2015 PASSED IN MVC NO.151/2010 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE,
MACT, KADUR, CHIKMAGALUR DISTRICT, AWARDING COMPENSATION OF Rs.3,33,234/- WITH INTEREST @ 8% P.A FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL THE DATE OF DEPOSIT AND ETC.
 THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsels appearing for the parties on both sides, the case is taken-up for final disposal.

2. This appeal is filed by Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC), Mysore Rural Division, Mysore ('Corporation' for short), challenging the judgment and award dated 22.07.2015 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT at Kadur, Chikmagalur District ('Tribunal' for short) in MVC No.151/2010 by partly allowing the claim petition filed by the petitioner/claimant and awarding compensation of Rs.3,33,234/- with interest at 8% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment.

3. In this appeal the Corporation has sought for setting aside the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal on the ground that said impugned judgment and award is erroneous in law and the same is opposed to facts, evidence, probabilities and circumstances of the case.

4. The brief facts of the case are that, on 15.07.2010 the claimant was riding his motor cycle bearing No.KA.18.K.3005 on the left side of the road from Haruvanahalli Village towards Kadur Town by The Division Controller vs Sri. Srinivasa on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194128807/
2 observing all Traffic Rules and Regulations and when he reached near MRM Oil Mill on NH 206 Road, Kadur Town, a KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.09.F.3673 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, dashed to the motor cycle.

As a result, the claimant sustained injuries and immediately he was shifted to Government Hospital at Kadur and thereafter, for better treatment, he was shifted to Nanjappa Hospital, Shimoga and admitted therein as inpatient from 15.07.2010 to 17.07.2010 and spent a huge amount for his treatment and as such he claimed compensation of Rs.10,50,000/- with interest.
Thereafter, on notice, the Corporation entered its appearance and filed written statement denying the averments made in claim petition, and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
5. In support of his case, the claimant has examined himself as PW.1 and produced documents at Exs.P1 to P26.

The Driver of the bus was examined as RW.1-M.D. Shekar and produced document as Ex.R1, which is the certified copy of judgment in CC No.694/2010 before the Court of Principal Civil Judge and JMFC at Kadur, whereby on appreciation of the evidence produced before it, the said Court has acquitted the accused of the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 338 of IPC vide judgment dated 06.06.2011 on the ground of production of insufficient oral and documentary evidence by the prosecution against accused/Driver-RW.1 and held that since there is no satisfactory evidence to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Further, the Doctor who treated the claimant,
was also examined through Court Commissioner as CW.1 and produced the documents marked as Ex.C1 to C6.

On appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence produced by the counsels on both sides, has allowed the claim petition partly and awarded compensation of Rs.3,33,234/- with interest at 8% per annum.
6. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant- Corporation and the learned counsel for the respondent No.1/claimant.
Perused the records.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant/Corporation submits that the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on higher side.

It is evident from the records that, the claimant has suffered Superficial Laceration over the left dorsum of foot measuring 4cmx1cmx0.5 cm; abrasion over the right big toe; and 2cmx2cm right temporal contusion.
He is stated to be aged 35 years and doing coconut business and he is also an agriculturist and earning a sum of Rs.10,000/- p.m.
The Doctor who treated the claimant has assessed the permanent disability at 25% to the limb, which is on higher side and it may be reduced.

Further he has also contended that, the accident has occurred in the year 2011 and therefore, in the absence of any material evidence, the Tribunal has taken the monthly income at Rs.4,500/-, which is on higher side and the same is to be reduced.
Further, the learned counsel has also contended that the amount awarded under other heads is also on higher side and hence, the same is required to be reduced.

8. Learned counsel for the respondent/claimant has sought to justify the impugned judgment and award passed by the tribunal contending that the claimant has suffered grievous injuries including head injury and to that effect he examined the CW.1-Dr. Narayana Panaji, who is the Neuro Surgeon of Nanjappa Hospital, Shimoga and the said Doctor, who has stated that he has treated the petitioner for injuries sustained by the petitioner and to that effect the claimant has also produced Exs. C1 to C6 and particularly C6 is a certificate issued by Manasa Nursing Home, Shimoga and the said document discloses that the disability suffered by the claimant is ranging from 50% to 70%.

The Division Controller vs Sri. Srinivasa on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194128807/
3
Therefore, the disability assessed by the Tribunal at 25% to whole body is just and proper and as such he prays to confirm the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

9. Having heard the arguments and on perusing the records, it is clear that, the Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the claimant at Rs.4,500/-, as the claimant has not produced any document in support of his contention and awarded compensation under the following heads:-

2 Medical Expenses 45,834/-
 3 Conveyance/Travelling Charges 4,900/-
 4 Attendant Charges and Nutritious 3,000/-
 Food

5 Loss of Income 13,500/-
 6 Future Loss of Income 2,16,000/-
 7

Future Medical Expenses 10,000/-
 8 Discomfort and loss of amenities 10,000/-
 of life
As stated above, the learned counsel for the appellant submits that the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on higher side.
It is argued that the claimant had not sustained 25% physical disability to whole body, but, he had suffered 25% disability to particular limb.
Therefore, the Tribunal is wrong in taking 25% disability to whole body.

But, in examination of CW.1 -Dr. Narayana Panaji, who is Neuro Surgeon of Nanjappa Hospital, Shimoga has deposed that, he has treated the petitioner in connection with injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident dated 15.07.2010 and after brain scanning, he has noticed the head injury and clotting of blood in the brain of petitioner.

He has also stated that the petitioner has suffered mental disorder and is having 25%
disability.
He has identified the relevant medical records of the petitioner maintained in their hospital as per Exs.C1 to C6.
Ex.C6 is a certificate issued by Manasa Nursing Home, Shimoga.
The said document discloses that the concerned psychiatrist and psychologist have estimated the mental score of the petitioner at 11.
The said document further discloses that the said disability ranges from 40% to 70%.

Hence, it appears that the above said disability relates to brain and which causes mental imbalance and the mental disorder also affects the regular physical function of the petitioner and as such, it appears the doctor has assessed the permanent disability to the whole body of the The Division Controller vs Sri. Srinivasa on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194128807/
4 claimant at 25%.
Further, in the absence of any material evidence, the Tribunal has rightly - 10 - assessed the notional income of the claimant at Rs.4,500/- per month.
11. Further, alternatively the learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that, the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on lesser side and therefore, prays for enhancement of compensation.

Further, he contended that, even though the appellant has not filed any appeal seeking enhancement of compensation under Order 41 Rule 33 of CPC, this Court has got discretionary power to enhance the of compensation and in this regard he relied upon the judgment of this Court passed in MFA No.8449/2015 (MV-I) dated 19.10.2022 (National Insurance Co. Ltd. -Vs- Mr.Alwin Lobo), wherein the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court by invoking Order 41 rule 33 of C.P.C, has awarded just and reasonable compensation by observing that, it is settled law that in an appeal filed by the Insurance Company, the Court can invoke the provisions of Order 41 Rule 33 of CPC, if injustice is caused to the victim or deceased while - 11 - awarding compensation.

The relevant portion of the said judgment reads as under:-
"17.

Now, coming to the aspect of invoking Order 41, Rule 33 of C.P.C. to award just and reasonable compensation, it is settled law that in an appeal filed by the Insurance Company, the Court can invoke Order 41, Rule 33 of C.P.C., if injustice is caused to the victim or deceased while awarding compensation.
In the case on hand, it has to be noted that the Doctor, who has been examined as P.W.3 assessed the disability at 65% since, he had suffered injury to his head.

The Tribunal, while answering issue No.3, taken note of the wound certificate which is marked as Ex.P7, wherein the claimant has sustained lacerated wound over 3rd web space of the left foot and diffused contusion over right side of the head which are simple in nature and CT scan revealed extra dural haematoma and midline shift thin sub dural haematoma over right frontal convexity, sub arachnoid hemorrhage, multiple hemorrhage contusion over bilateral frontal, parietal and left temporal lobe with diffuse cerebral edema,
diastatic fracture of sagital and coronal suture on left side, comminuted fracture of right parietal bone, left sided facial palsy, right sided hemiparesis and all these injuries are grievous in nature.
When the - 12 - claimant has sustained number of injuries and the Doctor is also examined before the Tribunal

, the same is not accepted by the Tribunal and the Tribunal comes to the conclusion that the evidence of P.W.2 revealed that the petitioner has permanent disability at 50% to 75% and Ex.P12 referred by P.W.3 would reveal that petitioner has permanent physical disability at 65%.

But, without assigning any reason, the The Division Controller vs Sri. Srinivasa on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194128807/
5 Tribunal has reduced the disability to 25%.
In a case of head injury, the disability cannot be converted as like an injury to limb and the Court has to take the actual disability.

When the permanent disability is assessed at 65% by P.W.2 and considering the nature of injuries, the Tribunal lost sight of the nature of injuries and also the evidence on record, that too, when the expert has given the evidence.

Hence,
it is appropriate to take the disability at 65% and when the Tribunal has passed perverse order in accepting the disability, such perversity amounts to injustice to the injured.

Hence, it is a fit case to exercise the powers under Order 41, Rule 33 of C.P.C.
to enhance the compensation.
12. The facts and circumstances of the above said case are different from this case.
In the present case, the involvement of vehicles in the accident and sustaining - 13 - injuries by the claimant is not in dispute.
It is also not in dispute that the claimant has suffered fracture to his forehead skull resulting in blood clot.

The doctor examined as CW.1 has also stated that the claimant was admitted in the hospital and he has conducted surgery on the claimant and he further stated that his mental capacity is reduced due to neurological problem developed due to the accidental injury on his forehead and as such, he assessed the disability to the brain ranging 60% to 70% and stated that the claimant has suffered 25% psycho neuro disability and he has also issued the certificate to that effect.

13. In view of the above, the Tribunal is justified in taking permanent disability to the extent of 25% to whole body as per the opinion of the doctor and the same need not be disturbed, as mental disorderness would also affects other physical functions of the body also.

Further, in the absence of any material evidence on record, the notional income taken by the tribunal at Rs.4,500/- per - 14 - month is also just and proper and the tribunal has also rightly adopted multiplier of '16' and calculated compensation and hence, the compensation amounts awarded by the Tribunal under various heads are also just and proper and does not call for any interference.

14. Further, as stated above, the claimant has also prays for enhancement of compensation in exercise of discretionary power vested in appellate Court by invoking provision of Order 41 Rule 33 of CPC by placing reliance on the decision in Mr. Alwin Lobo's case cited supra.

As stated above, the facts in the said case disclose that, the claimant in the said case has suffered multiple fractural injuries to the brain and the doctor has assessed 65% disability to the whole body, but the tribunal has considered the at 20% disability.

Therefore, in this case this court cannot invoke the The Division Controller vs Sri. Srinivasa on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194128807/
6 provisions of Order 41 Rule 33 of CPC, since no injustice is caused to the claimant.

sentences.text: Therefore, in this case, no such grounds are available warranting this court to invoke the above said provisions.
- 15 - Therefore, the said decision in Mr. Alwin Lobo's case relied upon by the learned counsel for the respondent/claimant is not helpful to the claimant.
Hence, the compensation awarded by the tribunal appears to be just and proper and does not call for any interference by this Court.
15. In facts and circumstances of the case, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and as such, I do not find any good ground to reduce the compensation.
Hence, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER i) The appeal is dismissed.
 ii) The impugned judgment and award dated  22.07.2015 passed by Tribunal viz., the  Senior Civil Judge and MACT at Kadur,
Chikmagalur District in MVC No.151/2010, stands confirmed.
iii) The amount in deposit shall be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
